title: DISCOVER SERVICES YOU COULD SELL WITH CHATGPT
content:
You may have sellable skills that do not feel special because they are normal to you. This interview is designed to uncover useful work you can already do or could reasonably learn to do, then connect it to a customer who might want that work done.

The goal is not to produce a giant list of random side hustles. It is to identify a small number of service directions grounded in your actual experience, abilities, constraints, and interests.

WHAT CHATGPT SHOULD LOOK FOR
Useful clues can come from jobs, hobbies, household responsibilities, volunteer work, things people ask you for help with, software you know, equipment you understand, problems you routinely solve, and tasks you perform faster or more confidently than other people.

A service direction becomes more useful when it names both the work and the customer. "Virtual assistant" is broad. "Remote invoicing and accounts-receivable support for small home-service businesses" is much more specific.

HOW TO USE THIS
Paste the prompt below into ChatGPT and answer the interview based on what you have actually done. Do not dismiss an ability just because it seems ordinary.

COPY & PASTE INTO CHATGPT

During the interview:
- Ask one question at a time unless a small group of tightly related questions is genuinely easier to answer together.
- Use my answers before deciding what to ask next.
- If I say "I don't know," help me identify what I need to decide or research rather than inventing an answer.
- Explain unfamiliar business terms in plain language.
- Separate assumptions from facts that require outside verification.
- Do not give me a generic list of businesses before learning about me.

Interview me to discover services I could realistically sell. Ask about my work history, responsibilities, hobbies, tools and software I know, practical skills, creative skills, technical skills, things people ask me for help with, problems I solve repeatedly, tasks I enjoy or tolerate, tasks I dislike, whether I prefer local or remote work, how much direct customer contact I want, my available time, and any constraints that matter.

Look beneath job titles for individual tasks and abilities. Help me distinguish between something I am merely familiar with and something I can responsibly perform for a customer.

When a possible service involves regulated work, licensing, insurance, certification, or other consequential requirements, flag that for independent verification rather than assuming I am allowed or qualified to provide it.

Narrow the possibilities instead of giving me dozens of ideas.

At the end give me:
- 3 to 5 strongest service directions
- The specific work involved in each
- The customer who might need it
- Why each fits my existing abilities or constraints
- Important skill gaps or external requirements to verify
- Which direction appears strongest based on my answers and why

WHERE TO GO NEXT
Choose the strongest direction you want to investigate and continue to PDF 42.
